title: Introduce congestion-pacing and structured fncall failsafe in gateway to stabilize streaming and OpenAI-compat
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Gateway: add congestion pacing to streaming proxy and a structured-function-call failsafe. Improves stability for long-lived OpenAI-compat streams and reduces noisy retries. No public API contract changes; internal routing and buffering knobs added.
description: Motivation: We see a recurring class of incidents where downstream model hosts or network egress introduce transient stalls that cause the gateway streaming proxy to retry/choke, which in turn amplifies tail latency and leads to degraded fncall/tool-call behavior in OpenAI-compat mode. This PR introduces a lightweight congestion-pacing layer in the streaming proxy plus a structured fncall failsafe that gracefully degrades tool call sequences when streaming is unstable. Summary of changes: 1) Add a congestion pacer (egress pacing token bucket + adaptive holdback) that smooths bursty egress from the proxy and prevents immediate retransmit storms; pacing parameters are workload-aware and derived from route profiles. 2) Add a fncall failsafe path: when the stream stalls beyond a configurable threshold, the gateway will atomically complete the structured function call with a best-effort buffered payload and mark the stream degraded via X-Redwood-Stream-Status header to allow clients to fallback. 3) Tighten route-level payload quotas and move per-route in-memory buffers into a capped slab allocator to avoid head-of-line OOMs. 4) Add observability: streaming pacing metrics, per-route degrade counters, and structured-fncall fallback histogram. 5) Tests: add unit and integration tests for pacing behavior, fncall fallback semantics, and OpenAI-compat regression tests. Backwards compatibility: The OpenAI-compat read/write semantics are preserved; clients will see a new response header when a fallback occurred. This is opt-in via route flag route_config.enable_stream_pacing (defaults to true for safety). Rollout plan: merge to main, canary to region-us-east-1 with routing weight 2% for 24h, monitor pacing_* metrics and structured_fncall_fallback_rate. If fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained for 1h, auto-rollback flag will be triggered. Implementation notes: the pacer lives in gateway/proxy/egress_pacer.rs and is invoked by the stream buffer loop; we selected an exponentially-smoothed target rate using recent egress success latency. The fncall failsafe reuses the existing structured-output serializer but forces a close-of-stream marker and emits a synthetic function-complete event to ensure downstream consumers (and SDKs) receive a final consistent payload. Testing summary: unit tests cover edge cases (zero-sized payloads, rapid connect/disconnect), e2e integration runs against a model simulator that flips egress stalls; local perf lab shows 18-34% reduction in tail retry storms. CI: all checks passed after two reruns of the flaky e2e streaming test. Docs: brief entry added to docs/openai_compat.md explaining the header and route flag. Related work: follows up on ENG-1304 (streaming robustness) and pairs with the canary autoscaler circuit from ENG-1421. If anything is unclear reach out to @priya for design walkthrough.
